facts.fact: PanIN is a microscopic, noninvasive duct lesion, usually under 0.5 cm, of cuboidal-to-columnar cells with variable apical mucin; epithelium almost always gastric-foveolar, flat or micropapillary.
facts.value: size <0.5 cm; flat or (micro)papillary; apical mucin
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Old three-tier grading: PanIN-1A flat and 1B micropapillary with minimal atypia and no mitoses; PanIN-2 pseudostratification, moderate atypia, hyperchromasia; PanIN-3 marked atypia, atypical mitoses, loss of polarity, cribriform or budding, necrosis possible.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Current two-tier system: low-grade = former PanIN-1A/1B and PanIN-2; high-grade = former PanIN-3 ('carcinoma in situ'). High-grade PanIN is found almost only alongside invasive PDAC.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: PanIN found in 82% of pancreata with PDAC, 60% with chronic pancreatitis and 16% of normal pancreata; both sexes equal; incidence tends to rise with age.
facts.value: 82% PDAC / 60% CP / 16% normal; rises with age
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: PanINs lie more often in the head than the tail, are macroscopically invisible and not seen on imaging, but may cause stricture with upstream duct dilation, lobular atrophy and fibrosis.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Table of precursors: PanIN location head = tail, size <0.5 cm; early KRAS and CDKN2A, late TP53 and SMAD4 changes.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 119 Molecular Understanding of the Development of Ductal Pancreatic Cancer (Lee, Hruban, Wood)

facts.fact: PanINs described as microscopic asymptomatic lesions of the terminal ductules (periphery of ductal tree) that progress to invasion most readily in head and uncinate process; 5-year survival after resection of resulting cancer 15-20%.
facts.book: Hingorani SR. Location, Location, Location: Precursors and Prognoses for Pancreatic Cancer. Gastroenterology 133(1):345-350
facts.chapter: Editorial text and Table 1

facts.fact: Invasive cancer is thought to arise from PanIN in small ducts: shared genetics, PanIN beside carcinoma, mouse models. Telomere shortening and KRAS early; CDKN2A mid; TP53, SMAD4, BRCA2 late; accumulation matters more than order.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: KRAS mutated in >90% of low- and high-grade PanIN; telomere shortening near-universal incl. PanIN-1A; GNAS in a subset; CDKN2A loss later; TP53 and SMAD4 late, SMAD4 perhaps only after invasion; PanIN lacks MUC2.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: High-grade PanIN is hard to tell from 'cancerization' of a duct by invasive carcinoma; abrupt transition from normal to highly atypical epithelium in one duct with adjacent invasive tumor favors cancerization.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Rare PanIN variants: foamy gland, intestinal and oncocytic types; the last two may be early IPMN or IOPN.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Mouse lineage-tracing: acinar cells undergo acinar-to-ductal metaplasia then PanIN then PDAC when Kras is mutated with inflammation; duct-derived tumors tended to bypass PanIN. Animal data, not shown in humans.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 120 From Tissue Turnover to the Cell of Origin of Pancreatic Cancer (Kong, Thoma, Michalski)

facts.fact: IPMN: grossly visible, usually papillary, noninvasive mucin-producing neoplasm of main or branch ducts, usually >=1.0 cm. A lesion 0.5-1.0 cm is large PanIN or small IPMN.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: IPMN sits most often in proximal gland (head, uncinate). Pooled invasive carcinoma: 43.6% main-duct, 16.6% branch-duct, 45.3% mixed. Duct-type split is mainly an imaging classification.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Main-duct involvement (main-duct or mixed IPMN) means main duct dilated to more than 5 mm, focal or diffuse; short segments can look cystic. Gaping 'fish-mouth' papilla may extrude mucus.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 84 Evaluation of Cystic Lesions Using EUS, MRI, and CT

facts.fact: Branch-duct IPMN shows as cysts over 10 mm that communicate with a non-dilated main duct; main-duct and mixed types have segmental or diffuse main duct dilation over 5 mm.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: Consensus risk tiers: main duct 5-9 mm is a worrisome feature; main duct >10 mm or enhancing mural nodule >5 mm is a high-risk stigma; cyst >3 cm worrisome.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: Imaging risk of high-grade dysplasia or invasion: cyst >3 cm (OR 2.97), main duct dilation (OR 2.4), mural nodule (OR 7.7); nodule size cut-offs vary from >=3 mm to >10 mm.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 84 Evaluation of Cystic Lesions Using EUS, MRI, and CT

facts.fact: Gross: main-duct IPMN diffusely dilates main duct, with long finger-like papillae and thick tenacious mucin; branch-duct IPMN is a grape-like cluster of cysts beside the main duct; many are mixed.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Branch-duct IPMN: multiple cystic dilations ('grape-like'), more often head/neck and uncinate process; IPMN mean age ~65, more men, mostly solitary and in the head, 20-40% multifocal.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 81 Histologic Classification and Staging of Cystic Neoplasms (Fukushima, Zamboni)

facts.fact: IPMN involves larger ducts, is commoner in men and more often in head than tail; 10-20% multifocal; lacks ovarian stroma and involves a duct (vs MCN). Mutations: GNAS, KRAS, TP53, SMAD4, RNF43.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Gastric-type IPMN (commonest): monolayer of columnar cells, basal nuclei, abundant mucin; flat, papillary or tubular; mostly branch ducts; usually low-grade, lowest invasion risk.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Intestinal-type IPMN resembles colonic villous adenoma: long branching papillae, elongated 'cigar' nuclei, goblet cells, MUC2/CDX2; usually high-grade and in the main duct. Pancreatobiliary-type: mucin-poor cells, irregular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, arborizing, mostly high-grade, most often invasive.
facts.value: intestinal: main duct; pancreatobiliary: arborizing HG
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Oncocytic IPMN is now a separate entity (IOPN): arborizing papillae of 1-5 layers of eosinophilic cells with prominent nucleoli and punched-out spaces; mean size 4.6-6 cm; ~2/3 in head; lacks KRAS/GNAS; PRKACA/PRKACB fusions.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Low-grade IPMN dysplasia: single layer of small uniform nuclei on well-formed papillae. High-grade: loss of polarity, hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei, irregular papillae, cribriform growth. About one-third of resected IPMN carry invasive PDAC.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Intestinal-type IPMN gives colloid (mucinous noncystic) carcinoma: mucin pools dissect stroma with neoplastic cells floating. Pancreatobiliary and some gastric types give tubular carcinoma like PDAC.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Colloid carcinoma from intestinal IPMN has better prognosis than PDAC (median survival 107 vs 20 months); tubular carcinoma from gastric branch-duct IPMN median 45 months.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: KRAS and GNAS each altered in 50-80% of IPMN, often together; RNF43 14-75%; CDKN2A common; TP53 in high-grade; SMAD4 usually only once invasive; KLF4 in low-grade. Average 26 mutations per IPMN.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Cysts appear in >2% of asymptomatic imaging cohorts, >80% IPMN; cysts and IPMN reach 13.5% and 12.2% after age 80. Resected 5-year survival 94% high-grade vs 31% invasive.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: IPMN usually in head, 7th-8th decade, men:women 1.5:1; Br-IPMN series of 145 resections: 46% adenoma, 32% borderline, 11% in situ, 11% invasive; expectant care suggested for branch lesions <3 cm without nodule or duct dilation.
facts.book: Hingorani SR. Location, Location, Location: Precursors and Prognoses for Pancreatic Cancer. Gastroenterology 133(1):345-350
facts.chapter: Editorial text and Table 1

facts.fact: Illustration: IPMN of pancreatic head with papillary tumor distending the main pancreatic duct and extending into smaller ducts and ductules.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: MCN: mostly perimenopausal women, body/tail, solitary, 'cyst-in-cyst' septated growth, no communication with the duct system; ovarian-type stroma is mandatory. Median size 3.5-5 cm (range 0.5-20 cm).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: MCN: men:women 1:10-20; >90% in body-tail; mean age ~45; round, smooth lining, fibrous pseudocapsule, frequent calcification; 2-35 cm; unilocular or multilocular; papillae or mural nodules track with malignancy.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 81 Histologic Classification and Staging of Cystic Neoplasms (Fukushima, Zamboni)

facts.fact: MCN: perimenopausal women, median age 48; >90% distal body or tail; mean size 6.5 cm; thick wall, no duct communication; 15-20% harbor focal invasive carcinoma.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: Lining ranges from flat/cuboidal cells with little mucin to tall columnar with supranuclear mucin; low- and high-grade areas coexist; denuded epithelium common. Ovarian-type stroma: spindle cells, estrogen/progesterone receptor positive, luteinized cells inhibin-positive.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: MCN genetics: average 16 coding mutations; KRAS hotspots (up to 100% in high-grade/invasive), RNF43; TP53 and CDKN2A in ~half of high-grade/invasive; GNAS absent, which separates MCN from IPMN.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Noninvasive MCN patients are about 10 years younger than invasive (44 vs 55 years); invasive carcinoma in 6-25% of resected MCN; 5-year disease-specific survival 57-79.6%.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: ~95% of MCN arise in women, usually in the tail, painless slow-growing; cysts larger than serous; thick tenacious mucin; columnar mucinous lining over dense ovarian-like stroma; up to a third have invasive carcinoma.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: MCN lies in periphery of body/tail, 5th decade, women:men 10-20:1, stroma with wavy nuclei and hormone receptors; typically no contiguity with duct system (may arise from terminal ductules).
facts.book: Hingorani SR. Location, Location, Location: Precursors and Prognoses for Pancreatic Cancer. Gastroenterology 133(1):345-350
facts.chapter: Editorial text and Table 1

facts.fact: Proposed origin: primordial germ cells or ovarian-type tissue stranded in pancreatic body/tail during embryonic descent; mechanism still unknown.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Serous cystic neoplasm: multicystic, usually in the tail, cysts 1-3 mm with glycogen-rich cuboidal cells and clear straw-coloured fluid; ~25% of cystic neoplasms; women 2:1; 6th-7th decade; VHL inactivation; benign.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Serous cystic neoplasms are typically in body and tail; mean size 4-6 cm at diagnosis; growth ~0.6 cm/year; mostly sporadic, multiple in VHL; no KRAS/RNF43/TP53 mutations.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: Serous cystadenoma: sponge-like microcystic mass with central scar; monolayer of clear glycogen-rich cells, central round nuclei; no duct communication; F:M 7:3, mean age 60; VHL mutation in 50% of sporadic.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 81 Histologic Classification and Staging of Cystic Neoplasms (Fukushima, Zamboni)

facts.fact: Serous cystadenoma may be microcystic (innumerable mm cysts around central scar), macrocystic (one or few large cysts) or solid; multiple lesions suggest VHL.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Solid-pseudopapillary neoplasm: mainly young women; large, well-circumscribed, solid and cystic with hemorrhagic debris; poorly cohesive cells in sheets or pseudopapillae; CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) mutation; usually cured by resection.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: SPN: median age 30, mean size 8 cm, body/tail in 60%, tail most frequent; CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations 83-100%; ~6% locally advanced, 8% distant metastases at presentation.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 86 Natural History of Cystic Neoplasms: IPMN, MCN, SCN, and SPN (Klotz, Hackert, Buchler)

facts.fact: SPN occurs with equal frequency in head, body and tail; large, well-demarcated, solid or cystic with hemorrhage and necrosis; monomorphic clear-cytoplasm cells on pseudopapillae; nuclear beta-catenin.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: ITPN: rare, solid noncystic intraductal tumor, little mucin; sexes equal; slight head predominance, about a quarter diffuse; back-to-back tubules of cuboidal cells with high-grade nuclei and comedo necrosis; up to 80% have invasion; lacks KRAS/GNAS.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 126 Pancreatic Cancer: Precancerous Lesions (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens)

facts.fact: Pseudocysts lack epithelial lining, are ~75% of pancreatic cysts, 2-30 cm, lined by fibrin and granulation tissue, often in lesser sac or retroperitoneum after pancreatitis.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: About 60% of pancreatic cancers arise in the head, 15% in the body, 5% in the tail, and 20% diffusely involve the gland.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: About 25% of PDAC present in body or tail; these are larger and more often metastatic (>4 cm: head 21%, body 40%, tail 51%; metastatic: head 42%, body 69%, tail 84%); <15% resectable.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 137 Left Pancreatectomy for Body and Tail Cancer (van Hilst et al.)

facts.fact: Hard, stellate, gray-white ill-defined masses. Head tumors obstruct the distal common bile duct (biliary distension in ~50%, most get jaundice); body/tail tumors stay silent, grow large, and are disseminated at discovery.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Cancer tracks along nerves, invades blood vessels and retroperitoneum, spleen, adrenals, colon, stomach; peripancreatic, gastric, mesenteric, omental and portohepatic nodes often involved; distant spread chiefly liver and lungs.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Malignant glands are poorly formed, lined by pleomorphic cuboidal to columnar cells, in an intense desmoplastic reaction; dense fibrosis can hinder biopsy as much tissue is nonneoplastic; perineural, lymphatic and large-vessel invasion common.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Gross: white-gray sclerotic firm mass infiltrating soft yellow lobulated parenchyma; invades or obstructs common bile duct and/or main duct, with upstream duct dilation and fibrous atrophy; most in head, then body/tail.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Haphazard glands in dense desmoplastic stroma; perineural and intravascular invasion in practically all cases; cells may spread along vessel endothelium or inside ducts ('cancerization'). Benign mimics keep lobular architecture.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 125 Pathology of Exocrine Pancreatic Tumors (Pittman, Hruban)

facts.fact: Perineural invasion occurs in almost all cases and tracks with severe pain (pain ~70%); head tumors cause painless jaundice, body/tail rarely; proximity to portal vein, celiac trunk and SMA means small tumors may invade vessels.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 127 Clinical History and Risk Factors of Pancreatic Cancer (Huser, Assfalg, Friess)

facts.fact: At diagnosis only 15-20% are resectable; 40-50% metastatic; 30-40% locally advanced (vascular involvement). Head/uncinate tumors present early with jaundice; neck/body with celiac plexus pain; tail late.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 134 Clinical Assessment and Staging of Advanced Pancreatic Cancer (Lindberg et al.)

facts.fact: Body/tail criteria (NCCN 2.2021, table garbled in extraction): borderline includes >180 degrees PV/SMV contact or celiac contact without aortic involvement; locally advanced is SMA contact >180 degrees, celiac plus aorta, unreconstructible PV/SMV.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 137 Left Pancreatectomy for Body and Tail Cancer (van Hilst et al.)

facts.fact: EUS identified a mass in 70% of patients with indeterminate CT; mean tumor size 21 mm in that series (not a general size at diagnosis).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 134 Clinical Assessment and Staging of Advanced Pancreatic Cancer (Lindberg et al.)

facts.fact: Imaging hallmarks: upstream pancreatic atrophy, abrupt main-duct cutoff with dilation, biliary dilation in head tumors; 'double duct sign' when both bile and pancreatic ducts dilate.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 129 Radiologic Diagnosis of Pancreatic Cancer: CT, MRI

facts.fact: Gene alterations in PDAC: KRAS activating mutation 90-95%, CDKN2A 95% (most frequent tumor suppressor), SMAD4 55%, TP53 70-75% in text (table says 50-70%).
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: KRAS >90% (codons 12, 13, 61); CDKN2A ~90% (about 40% mutation+LOH, 40% homozygous deletion, 10-15% methylation); TP53 ~75%; SMAD4 ~55%; MSI 2-3%.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 119 Molecular Understanding of the Development of Ductal Pancreatic Cancer (Lee, Hruban, Wood)

facts.fact: Five-year survival ~10% in US; resected 15-25%; only ~33% present with local disease; most cases after age 60, sexes equal; smoking RR ~1.7, ~20% attributable.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 117 Epidemiology of Pancreatic Cancer (Mocci, Klein)

facts.fact: Pancreatic cancer five-year survival is under 5% (2013-era data in this edition).
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: 80% of pancreatic cancers occur at ages 60-80; cigarette smoking is thought to double risk; chronic pancreatitis and diabetes are both risk factors and consequences.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Five-year survival 39%, 13% and 3% for localized, regional and distant disease; over 80% unresectable at first diagnosis (per chapter).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 133 The Role of Laparoscopy and Peritoneal Cytology in the Management of Pancreatic Cancer

facts.fact: About 70% of human pancreatic cells are acinar and 18.5% ductal; PDAC arises from exocrine cells (acinar via ADM/PanIN in mice, ductal also possible).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 120 From Tissue Turnover to the Cell of Origin of Pancreatic Cancer (Kong, Thoma, Michalski)

facts.fact: Stromal cells (activated pancreatic stellate cells = cancer-associated fibroblasts) drive desmoplasia from PanIN stage through metastases; they make collagen and fibronectin.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 123 Tumor Microenvironment: Immune Cells and Immunosuppressive Functions of CAFs and Macrophages

facts.fact: Reported para-aortic node metastasis 16% and 26% in head cancer, 13% and 17% in body/tail cancer; at least 12 regional nodes needed for staging.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 135 Pancreatic Cancer: Indications for Resection

facts.fact: PanNETs are ~2% of pancreatic neoplasms, occur anywhere along the gland or peripancreatic tissue; solitary ones often <2 cm, encapsulated, pale to red-brown; look like giant islets; insulinoma amyloid common.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 24 The Endocrine System

facts.fact: Insulinoma is most common, ~90% benign; 60-90% of other PanNETs malignant; gastrinomas arise in duodenum and pancreas; sporadic alterations in MEN1, PTEN/TSC2, ATRX/DAXX (nearly half).
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 24 The Endocrine System

facts.fact: PanNETs arise in all parts of pancreas; size 0.5-20 cm; insulinomas usually <2 cm, nonfunctioning larger; <5 mm = microtumors; functioning <40% of PanNETs; MEN1 30-70% develop them.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 99 Pathology of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (Kasajima, Sasano)

facts.fact: PanNETs <3% of pancreatic tumors; incidence <1/100,000; insulinoma malignancy <10%, gastrinoma and others >50%.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 98 Epidemiology and Classification of Neuroendocrine Tumors of the Pancreas

facts.fact: Western incidence 10-20 per 100,000; biliary disease and alcohol cause ~80%; gallstones in 35-60%; ~5% of gallstone patients get pancreatitis; alcohol share 65% US, 20% Sweden, <=5% S. France/UK.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Three initiating routes: duct obstruction, primary acinar injury, defective intracellular proenzyme transport; trypsin activates prophospholipase and proelastase; lipase active, causes fat necrosis; edema and small-vessel thrombosis amplify injury.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Interstitial form: mild inflammation, edema, focal fat necrosis (fatty acids + calcium = soaps, granular blue). Necrotizing form: acinar, ductal and islet necrosis, red-black hemorrhagic gland with chalky fat necrosis, also in omentum and mesentery.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: ~5% of severe cases die in week one; 40-60% of necrotizing cases become infected; sequelae include sterile abscess and pseudocyst.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Acute interstitial edematous pancreatitis affects 90-95% of patients; necrotizing 5-10%. Mild form often gallstone-related, severe form usually alcohol-related; fat necrosis (autodigestive) is the commonest pattern.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 17 Histopathology of Acute Pancreatitis (Kloppel)

facts.fact: Fat necroses in interstitial disease are tiny (<10 mm) white spots; necrotizing disease has large confluent peripancreatic fat necrosis, hemorrhage when veins involved; necrosis 2-5 cm can resorb, >5 cm walls off by 20-30 days.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 17 Histopathology of Acute Pancreatitis (Kloppel)

facts.fact: Acinar cells beside fat necrosis stay preserved, islets spared unless the lobule is necrotic; acinar necrosis as first lesion is not proven in common causes.
facts.value: acinar necrosis not proven as initiator
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 17 Histopathology of Acute Pancreatitis (Kloppel)

facts.fact: Only about 5% or fewer heavy drinkers develop pancreatitis; diagnosis usually needs ~80-100 g alcohol daily for at least 5 years.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 11 Epidemiology and Etiology of Alcohol-Induced Pancreatitis (Wilson et al.)

facts.fact: Genes: PRSS1 (gain of function), SPINK1 (loss), CFTR, CASR, CTRC and CPA1 raise risk of pancreatitis; mutations act by raising trypsin activity or duct plugging.
facts.value: PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR, CASR, CTRC, CPA1
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Chronic pancreatitis: fibrosis, acinar dropout and variable duct dilation; hard gland with dilated ducts and calcified concretions; epithelium atrophic, hyperplastic or squamous-metaplastic; islets relatively spared, may fuse and look enlarged, lost in advanced disease.
facts.value: fibrosis + acinar loss; islets spared early
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Most common cause is long-term alcohol; also duct obstruction, autoimmune, hereditary (up to 25% genetic); alcoholic type shows ductal dilatation with protein plugs and calcifications; stellate cells driven by TGF-beta and PDGF lay down collagen.
facts.value: alcohol most common; genetic up to 25%
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Chronic pancreatitis: 20-25-year mortality 50%; pseudocysts in ~10%; hereditary pancreatitis carries 40% lifetime pancreatic cancer risk.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Hereditary pancreatitis genes: PRSS1 gain-of-function (dominant), SPINK1 loss (recessive), CFTR, also CASR, CTRC, CPA1; CFTR loss lowers bicarbonate and promotes protein plugs.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Inherited cancer risk table: hereditary pancreatitis (PRSS1, SPINK1) gives 50-80-fold risk, 25-40% by age 70.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 19 The Pancreas

facts.fact: Gland becomes firm, shrunken with irregular contour; dilated duct from stricture or intraductal stones; fibrosis blurs lobulation; strictures, stones, pseudocysts, vascular complications typical.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 52 Structural Complications: Strictures, Stones, Pseudocysts, and Vascular Complications (Tian et al.)

facts.fact: Duct stones in ~50% (50% at 5 years, nearly 100% by 14 years); bile duct stricture 3-46%; pseudocysts 20-40%; groove pancreatitis ~5%; vascular complications 8.4-12.2% (splenic vein thrombosis commonest).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 52 Structural Complications: Strictures, Stones, Pseudocysts, and Vascular Complications (Tian et al.)

facts.fact: Mechanistic definition: fibro-inflammatory syndrome with persistent response to injury; established features atrophy, fibrosis, duct distortion/strictures, calcification, exocrine and endocrine failure, dysplasia; five stages from at-risk to end-stage.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 38 Definition and Classification of Chronic Pancreatitis (Whitcomb)

facts.fact: Hereditary pancreatitis: acute pancreatitis median onset 10-12 years, chronic by 2nd-3rd decade, ~50% lifetime cumulative; PRSS1 penetrance ~80% (93% in France); SPINK1, CFTR, CTRC also.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 45 Hereditary Pancreatitis and Complex Genetic Causes (Ohlsen, Whitcomb)

facts.fact: Cancer risk in chronic pancreatitis: pooled RR 12.0 (definite CP), 69 (hereditary), 14.4 in first cohort; cumulative incidence 4% over 20 years.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 61 Pancreatic Cancer Risks in Chronic Pancreatitis (Maisonneuve, Lowenfels)

facts.fact: Stellate cells are 4-7% of parenchymal cells, periacinar with vitamin A droplets; injury activates them to alpha-SMA myofibroblasts that make excess collagen.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 9 Fibrogenesis in the Pancreas: The Role of Pancreatic Stellate Cells (Apte et al.)

facts.fact: Diabetes occurs in 70% of chronic pancreatitis patients; most are insulin deficient.
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 10 Pancreatic Endocrine-Exocrine Relationship (Furuyama, Kawaguchi)

facts.fact: Type 1 diabetes shows classic features only after >90% of beta cells are destroyed; CD8+ cytotoxic T cells and TH1 cytokines injure beta cells; autoantigens insulin, GAD, ICA512.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 24 The Endocrine System

facts.fact: Type 1: fewer, smaller islets; uneven insulitis of mostly T lymphocytes may persist at presentation. Type 2: subtle islet loss; amyloid starts around capillaries and between cells, can obliterate islets.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 24 The Endocrine System

facts.fact: Islet amyloid is characteristic of long-standing type 2 diabetes, found in >90% of diabetic islets; >80% of type 2 patients are obese.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 24 The Endocrine System

facts.fact: Islet amyloid is made of islet amyloid polypeptide (AIAPP); listed under endocrine amyloid in type 2 diabetes.
facts.book: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease (Kumar, Abbas, Aster)
facts.chapter: Ch 6 Diseases of the Immune System (amyloidosis)

facts.fact: At onset of type 1, beta-cell mass can be reduced by >90%; proliferation rises but cannot compensate; mass roughly unchanged in prediabetic phase.
facts.book: Molecular and Cell Biology of Pancreas Development, Function and Regeneration (Golson, ed.; Adv Anat Embryol Cell Biol vol 239)
facts.chapter: Ch 'beta-Cell Heterogeneity and Plasticity' (Yong, Wang)

facts.fact: Table: human beta-cell mass in diabetes reduced up to 90%; obesity raises mass 1.5-2-fold in humans.
facts.book: Molecular and Cell Biology of Pancreas Development, Function and Regeneration (Golson, ed.; Adv Anat Embryol Cell Biol vol 239)
facts.chapter: Ch 'beta-Cell Heterogeneity and Plasticity' (Yong, Wang)

facts.fact: In type 2 diabetes human beta-cell loss ranges 24-65% with smaller islets; degranulation and dedifferentiation to progenitor-like cells increased about threefold.
facts.book: Molecular and Cell Biology of Pancreas Development, Function and Regeneration (Golson, ed.; Adv Anat Embryol Cell Biol vol 239)
facts.chapter: Ch 'beta-Cell Heterogeneity and Plasticity' (Yong, Wang)

facts.fact: Exocrine changes: pancreas 45% smaller in type 1; fecal elastase-1 low in 31.8% of diabetics (type 1 37.7%, type 2 26.2%).
facts.book: The Pancreas: An Integrated Textbook of Basic Science, Medicine, and Surgery (Beger et al., eds)
facts.chapter: Ch 10 Pancreatic Endocrine-Exocrine Relationship (Furuyama, Kawaguchi)
